s: Featherweight pub/sub + request-reply bus with microsecond latency; JetStream adds persistence when needed.
w: Subject-based matching (foo.*.bar wildcards) routes messages without brokers storing them by default - pure fire-and-forget at insane speeds. JetStream streams persist with consumers, exactly-once opts, and retention policies. Clusters use Raft; super-clusters bridge regions. Single Go binary deploys anywhere.
use: Internal RPC replacement (request-reply semantics built in)
IoT/edge fleets where footprint matters (runs on ARM boxes)
Service discovery-ish broadcast (presence, config refresh signals)
avoid: Long-term archival/event-sourcing stores (JetStream exists but kafka ecosystem richer)
pits: Core NATS loses messages if no subscriber - decide persistence needs consciously (JetStream on/off)
tips: Position honestly: simplicity/speed vs kafka's durability ecosystem tradeoff
